title: /boxoffice has no network error handling — leaves interaction hanging
description:
bot.py:211-243 (/boxoffice) calls _bom_search and _bom_scrape_grosses via asyncio.to_thread but neither wraps requests.get in try/except. A network blip, BOM 5xx, or DNS failure raises requests.RequestException, which propagates out of the to_thread future. Since the interaction was already deferred, the user sees 'The application did not respond.'

/yearlytop10 already handles this correctly. /boxoffice should follow the same pattern: catch requests.RequestException around the _bom_search and _bom_scrape_grosses calls and send a 'Couldn't reach Box Office Mojo' followup.
close_reason: Wrapped _bom_search and _bom_scrape_grosses calls in /boxoffice with try/except requests.RequestException, matching the existing /yearlytop10 pattern. User now gets 'Couldn't reach Box Office Mojo. Try again later.' instead of a hanging interaction.

title: tree.sync() runs on every on_ready — burns daily sync quota
description:
bot.py:339 calls tree.sync() inside the on_ready handler. on_ready fires on every reconnect/session resume, but Discord's global slash-command sync is rate-limited to ~200/day. A bot that reconnects frequently can exhaust the quota and stop receiving new command updates.

The idiomatic discord.py fix is to move the sync into setup_hook (or a Client subclass), and only sync when commands actually change. As a quick fix, guard the sync with a 'synced' flag so it only runs once per process lifetime.
close_reason: Moved tree.sync() to a setup_hook on a minimal Client subclass; on_ready no longer triggers the sync. PR #3 opened against main.

title: Rewrite README to match current bot (commands, no TMDB, no Message Content Intent)
description:
The committed README described an older TMDB-based implementation with two commands, hyphenated command names, a setup step for a TMDB key, and instructions to enable Message Content Intent. Current bot.py implements four BOM-scraping slash commands (/ping, /boxoffice, /weekendtop10, /yearlytop10) with no TMDB dependency and uses Intents.default(). README rewrite needs to match reality.

Also fix:
- Reference to non-existent .env.example
- Reference to non-existent scrape_weekend_chart() function in troubleshooting
- Misleading guidance about Message Content Intent
- Missing /yearlytop10 documentation
close_reason: README rewritten on branch boxdoffice-40h; PR #2 opened against main.

title: HEADERS used at bot.py:37 before defined at bot.py:78
description:
_bom_search references the module-level HEADERS constant on line 37, but HEADERS is defined on line 78. This works only because Python resolves module globals at call time rather than definition time — so the function works at runtime, but the code is misleading to read and brittle against refactors that reorder definitions.

Move HEADERS (and any other shared constants) to the top of the module, above the helper functions that use them.

title: _weekend_url_candidates only tries 2 weeks — extend to 3
description:
bot.py:101-106 generates ISO-week URLs for the most recent Friday and one week prior. If BOM is missing the page for the most recent ISO week (rare but happens around holidays / late-publishing) AND the prior week, the user gets an empty followup.

Bump the candidate list from (0, -1) to (0, -1, -2) so we degrade more gracefully. Trade-off: slightly slower failure path when BOM is fully down (3 HTTP timeouts instead of 2).

title: asyncio.Lock around weekend_cache to dedupe concurrent cold-cache fetches
description:
bot.py:23-26 / get_weekend_chart: two /weekendtop10 invocations arriving within ms of each other while the cache is cold will both kick off _fetch_weekend_chart (two scrapes of BOM). Single-instance Python is GIL-protected so the dict mutation itself is safe, but the deduplication is missed.

Add an asyncio.Lock; on cache miss, acquire the lock, re-check the cache (double-checked locking), then fetch. Negligible overhead for warm-cache reads.

title: Stale test pycache and missing .pytest_cache/ in .gitignore
description:
__pycache__/test_bot.cpython-314-pytest-9.0.2.pyc exists but no test_bot.py is in the tree — leftover from deleted tests. Delete it. Also .pytest_cache/ is not in .gitignore (only __pycache__/ is), so pytest artifacts can leak into commits.

Add .pytest_cache/ to .gitignore and remove the stale .pyc.

title: Replace regex page-walk in _bom_scrape_grosses with CSS selectors
description:
bot.py:49-72 parses Domestic/International/Worldwide gross by splitting the entire page text into lines and pattern-matching a money regex near label lines. This works but is fragile against any structural change to the BOM title page — and the commit log (834e93c, 73a0a61) shows we have already iterated through column-index bugs.

Replace with CSS selectors against BOM performance summary structure (e.g. .mojo-performance-summary-table or similar — inspect live page). Tighter coupling to specific selectors, but more diagnosable when it breaks.

Not urgent; current code works. File this as polish for next time the parser breaks.

title: Use urllib.parse.quote instead of requests.utils.quote
description:
bot.py:36 uses requests.utils.quote to URL-encode the BOM search query. requests.utils.quote is just a re-export of urllib.parse.quote; calling stdlib directly is more idiomatic and avoids the implicit dependency on requests' internal helpers.

Trivial swap: from urllib.parse import quote.

title: Remove unused TMDB_API_KEY from local .env
description:
The local .env file (not committed) carries a TMDB_API_KEY left over from an earlier README that described a TMDB-based implementation. The current bot.py only reads DISCORD_TOKEN; the TMDB key is dead. Delete the line locally to avoid confusion.

The .env file is gitignored and was never committed (verified via git log).
